findings.title: Resource lookup uses wrong owner ID and fails to set resource type upon creation
findings.body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` (line 214) and `hasPermission(String)` (line 244), `resourceStore.findByName(server, ..., server.getId())` passes `server.getId()` (the internal UUID of the resource server) as the `ownerId`. However, when `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates a resource (line 104 of `AdminPermissionsSchema.java`), it passes `resourceServer.getClientId()` (`"admin-permissions"`) as the owner ID. Because `server.getId()` does not equal `server.getClientId()`, `findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())` will only find resources if the single-argument overload `findByName(server, name)` (which defaults ownerId to `server.getClientId()`) is used, or if `server.getId()` happens to match. Specifically, in `JPA` / `Infinispan` stores, `findByName(ResourceServer, String, String)` queries by `owner = ownerId`. Even more importantly, in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (line 104), newly created per-client resources do not have `resource.setType(resourceType)` called on them, which means `getClientsWithPermission` (line 138: `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`) will never find per-client resources because their `type` field is `null`.

findings.title: All-clients permission is not evaluated when a client resource exists for a different scope
findings.body: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)` (lines 214-234), if a resource for `client` exists in the `resourceStore` (for example, because a permission was created for `client` with the `map-roles` scope), `resource` is non-null. The method then evaluates permissions only against this specific client resource and never falls back to evaluating the `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` ("all-clients") resource. Consequently, if an admin has an "all-clients" permission granting `manage` or `view`, and a specific permission on `client` for `map-roles`, `hasPermission(client, "manage")` will return `false` instead of falling back to the all-clients permission (unless a negative policy on the specific client explicitly denies it, as handled in `UserPermissionsV2`).

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle CLIENTS resource type
findings.body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName(KeycloakSession, Policy, Resource)` (lines 304-326) only resolves human-readable resource names when `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)`, returning `"All users"` or `user.getUsername()`. It was not updated to handle `CLIENTS.getType()`, so for client permissions it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()` (which is null/UUID) instead of returning `"All clients"` or the client's `clientId`.
